Hi Vivek,

Hope you're well — procurement at Acme is starting the security sign-off for our expansion project and we need to collect Redwood's SOC 2 Type II materials. A couple of specific asks from our InfoSec team: 

- Do you have a current SOC 2 Type II report we can review? If so, please confirm the audit period.
- We need clarification on which deployment modes are covered by the SOC 2: Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem). Our primary concern is whether Dedicated pools provided by Redwood are considered in-scope by the report or if they require a bridge letter.
- If a bridge letter is recommended, can you provide a sample and confirm whether Private/VPC/on-prem deployments are covered or excluded (and what alternative evidence you can provide)?

Ideal timeline: procurement would like the artifacts by EOD Friday (2027-12-03) so security can kick off their review next week.

Thanks — feel free to loop in legal or compliance as needed.

Best,
Alice Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corporation

Team — forwarding Acme's procurement request. Quick notes and ask: 

- They want the Type II report and explicit coverage mapping by hosting mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC/on-prem).
- Assume we have a current Type II that covers the hosted control plane and multi-tenant runtime. Need to confirm whether Dedicated pools (reserved GPU clusters) were included in the auditor's scope or treated as a separate environment.
- Private/VPC is customer-managed network; we usually exclude on-prem turnkey installs from our Type II unless the customer is on Redwood Private with our managed control plane — confirm wording.

Action items:
- Kimberly: Can you pull the latest SOC 2 Type II PDF (auditor letter + control matrix) and highlight sections that reference Dedicated pools and routing/fallback behavior? Also confirm the exact audit period (start/end dates).
- Neha: If the auditor provided a bridge-letter template or statement for Dedicated pool inclusion, share a draft. If not, coordinate with Tom at SOCAudits to produce a short bridge letter stating applicability and any nascent exceptions.
- Monica: Prep a short summary (1 page) for procurement that explains how Dedicated pools differ operationally from Hosted (tenant isolation, dedicated hardware, sign-in flows) and list available compensating controls we can evidence.
- Marissa: If there's any redline language in contracts around SOC scope, please advise on acceptable wording for procurement.

Target: respond to Acme with materials by EOD 2027-12-01 so procurement has at least the report and a plan.

Thanks — Vivek

Hi Vivek / Kimberly / Neha,

Thanks for the ping. We issued Redwood's most recent SOC 2 Type II on 2027-07-01 covering the period 2026-07-01 through 2027-06-30. The issued report covers Redwood's hosted control plane and the multi-tenant runtime that was sampled during our examination. 

A few important clarifications from the audit perspective: 

- Dedicated pools: our audit included certain dedicated customer environments that were operated within Redwood-managed pools where tenant separation and access controls matched our sampling criteria. However, not all Dedicated configurations were sampled; when customers have dedicated hardware with isolation profiles that differ materially, we typically issue a bridge letter to extend applicability to specific dedicated pools and date ranges.

- Private / VPC / on-prem: these deployments are often out-of-scope of the standard SOC 2 because they rely on customer-managed networking and sometimes local operational processes. For Private with a Redwood-managed control plane (Redwood Private with our control plane still providing management and logging), we can evaluate inclusion on a case-by-case basis; otherwise, we recommend providing alternative evidence (configuration checklist, KMS attestation, HSM integration logs, and audit logs export) rather than treating on-prem installs as in-scope.

I attached a sample bridge-letter template for Dedicated pool inclusion (Redwood_bridgeletter_dedicated_sample_20271201.docx) and an evidence index CSV that maps controls to typical artifacts for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (evidence-index-hosted-dedicated.csv).

If Acme needs an auditor-signed bridge letter tailored to their Dedicated cluster, we can draft one once Redwood confirms which dedicated pool and the specific dates for which they want applicability extended. Typical turnaround for a signed bridge letter: 3–5 business days after we receive the requested control evidence and scope confirmation.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with Acme's InfoSec to walk through the coverage matrix and the evidence list — suggest Wed 2027-12-06 or Thu 2027-12-07.

Tom Rivera, CPA
Partner, SOCAudits LLC

Attachment(s): Redwood_bridgeletter_dedicated_sample_20271201.docx, evidence-index-hosted-dedicated.csv

Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II report + hosting-mode applicability (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Alice — thanks for the note and quick timeline. Attaching the current SOC 2 Type II report and a short summary to get you started. Key points up front: 

1) SOC 2 Type II report (attachment: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_20270630.pdf) — audit period 2026-07-01 through 2027-06-30 and covers the hosted control plane and sampled runtime instances.

2) Dedicated pools — covered conditionally. Our auditor (Tom) included sampled dedicated environments, but we typically issue a targeted bridge letter when a customer requests explicit applicability for a specific dedicated pool and date range. We've attached a sample bridge letter and an evidence-index that maps controls to artifacts you can review. If you want a signed auditor bridge letter for your Dedicated cluster, please confirm: cluster name/ID, date range to extend, and any configurations that deviate from our standard dedicated profile.

3) Private / VPC / on-prem — generally excluded from the standard Type II because of customer-managed components. If you're evaluating Redwood Private (Redwood-managed control plane in your VPC) we can review inclusion; otherwise we will provide an evidence bundle (KMS integration attestation, agent logging export, configuration checklist) to satisfy specific controls.

Next steps from Acme:
- Confirm whether you want an auditor-signed bridge letter for Dedicated and provide the dedicated cluster identifier and desired coverage dates.
- If Private/on-prem is in play, indicate whether Redwood will manage the control plane or if it's entirely customer-managed; we will prepare the appropriate artifacts.

We aim to have the bridge letter draft ready within 48 hours of scope confirmation and a signed version within 3–5 business days after Tom's team receives the evidence package.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_20270630.pdf; Redwood_bridgeletter_dedicated_sample_20271201.docx; evidence-index-hosted-dedicated.csv

Regards,
